candidates.original_title: Representing object colour in language comprehension
candidates.description: Sentence-picture verification task produces a mismatch advantage for color (faster responses when the picture color mismatches the implied color in the sentence)
candidates.citation_sentence: The first experiment was conducted as a conceptual replication of Connell's (2007) and Zwaan and Pecher's (2012) experiments on color, to resolve which of the contradicting findings has more empirical support.
candidates.notes: The replication found a match advantage (opposite direction from Connell's mismatch advantage), but the authors do not explicitly call this a reversal of Connell (2007); they frame it as supporting Zwaan & Pecher (2012) instead. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.description: Sentence-picture verification task produces a match advantage for color (faster responses when the picture color matches the implied color in the sentence)
candidates.citation_sentence: The first experiment was conducted as a conceptual replication of Connell's (2007) and Zwaan and Pecher's (2012) experiments on color, to resolve which of the contradicting findings has more empirical support.

candidates.original_title: Revisiting mental simulation in language comprehension: Six replication attempts
candidates.description: Sentence-picture verification task produces a match advantage for color
candidates.citation_sentence: Our current study explored how much sensory information is included in mental simulations by conducting four experiments, using the same experimental paradigm as Connell (2007) and Zwaan and Pecher (2012) where sentences are used to imply a certain color, followed by an object-verification task.
candidates.notes: Experiment 2a found no significant match advantage for accuracy (p = .331) or RTs (p = .801) when saturation was reduced to the lowest level at which hue was still recognizable. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]
